scoring_justification: The hidden reference SD spectrum is a known synthetic curve (the paper's computed spectrum). The checker recomputes expected signal at selected energies from hidden Gaussian parameters and compares the agent's interpolated signal using relative tolerance; this is a recompute-tier comparison but operates on the output CSV.

outputs.description: Normalized self-diffraction signal as a function of photon energy. The hidden checker compares the agent's curve to a digitized reference from the paper using structural checks and relative tolerances on specific energy points.

output_contract.notes: The agent must perform the full DFT+BSE pipeline and compute the SD signal curve. Only the theoretical model reproduction is targeted; the experimental measurement is excluded.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference SD spectrum parameters (Gaussian peaks) representing the paper's calculated spectrum (Figure 3).
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Synthetic analytic fixture generated to match the qualitative features (peak at M2,3 edge, shoulder, dip, higher peak) as described in the paper and produced by the reference solve.sh.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Combination of four Gaussians with centers, widths, and amplitudes chosen to reproduce a curve with main peak at 59 eV, shoulder at 61 eV, dip at 62.5 eV, and peak at 64 eV, normalized to maximum of 1.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The reference solution (solve.sh) writes this exact curve; the task's gold is the synthetic curve representing the paper's computed spectrum. The checker uses the same parameters to compute expected values.

steps.description: Structural checks: peak location in 58-60 eV, and maximum signal below 57 eV is less than 0.1 of the global maximum.
Relative accuracy of SD signal at hidden photon energies (55,58,59,60,62,64 eV) within a ±20% tolerance.
